scope.future_policy: Use invented successor identities after the historical cutoff. Research informs institutional career paths and party policy; it does not predict offices held by real people. Label fiction and preserve historical source facts.
scope.unrepresented_parties: DPJ/CDP, Nippon Ishin, DPP, Reiwa, Sanseito, the Conservative Party, New Socialist Party and other parties are not covered by the five 1990 simulation rows. Each needs a separate game identity before coverage can be claimed.
scope.claim: All five represented parties have real leaders identified at the 1990 start. This research does not claim complete world history, exhaustive Japanese chronology or finished avatars.

ingestion.people: Compatible with Person: id, name, native, born/died DateBound and sources.
ingestion.parties: Compatible with Party and Term. Replace existing Japan rows and merge people by exact ID while preserving office_links. Coverage is partial; do not promote uncertain month boundaries to exact dates.
ingestion.intervals: Term windows are half-open [from, until). End dates are normalized to the successor's start where a source gives an inclusive final day. Month/year bounds express uncertainty, not a known vacancy.
ingestion.affiliations: Only evidenced leadership windows are included. These are not complete party-membership histories.

boundary_review.issue: The official LDP history distinguishes selection from effective tenure: Koizumi to 30 September 2006 and Abe from 1 October, despite Abe's election on 20 September. Similar differences occur in 2009, 2012, 2021 and 2024. This staging file transcribes the listed effective term dates rather than silently substituting election or prime-ministerial dates.

Election, ratification and effective term dates can differ. Doi's September 1986 start, Tanabe's July 1991 start, the 2013 October handover and the 2020 February handover retain month precision until primary office-effective records resolve them.

The official party history puts Hamayotsu's assumption in January 1998, while some secondary chronologies give September 1997. Local Komei and national New Peace/New Komei were separate organizations.
The April 1990 congress spans 24–26 April in available accounts. The June 1994 handover remains at month precision. NDL item 27 confirms the dissolution congress on 9 December 1994.

source_quality.primary: Official party records, parliamentary/archival catalogs and contemporary event organizers are preferred. The NDL entries describe primary historical documents without implying the full documents were read.
source_quality.secondary: Named encyclopedia entries and broadcaster coverage support limited chronology when precise primary dates were not retrieved. Such boundaries retain month or year precision.
source_quality.not_verified: Photo copyright clearance, exhaustive biographical dates, complete memberships, acting periods and every minor split branch remain separate research tasks.
